Results at conditions 1-5 are broadly benefic; 6-8 are intermediate; 9-11 are adverse with condition 11 (Deep Debilitation) being classified as Rikta (Void); 16-17 are severely adverse. This matrix is the primary qualitative filter for all sign-based Dasa assessments.

full_text: In the Chara Dasa holistic audit specification: Sloka 86 establishes a mandatory pre-assessment step. This holistic audit requirement is a core engine specification that prevents over-reliance on any single-planet assessment.

full_text: In the Chara Dasa Kendradi magnitude logic: Sloka 87 establishes the result-magnitude rule based on the positional type of the Dasa lord. There are three positional categories relative to any reference point: Kendra (angular — 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th), Panaphara (succedent — 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th), and Apoklima (cadent — 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th). When the Dasa lord is in a Kendra position, the Dasa delivers its full promised effects at maximum intensity. In a Panaphara position, the effects are realised at medium or half-strength. In an Apoklima position, only minimal or small effects are produced — even strong Raja Yogas are downgraded to minor achievements if the Dasa lord is in an Apoklima. This is a mandatory magnitude-scaling rule that the engine must apply after qualitative assessment.

full_text: In the Chara Dasa temporal distribution engine: Slokas 88-89 establish the Rasi-type-based timing rule for when within a Dasa cycle its promised results will manifest. This temporal mapping is a critical engine parameter that determines not just whether an event occurs but when within the Dasa it manifests. The engine must apply this Rasi-type classification before generating timing predictions.

The 12 Antardasas proceed through the 12 Rasis in order starting from this lord-placement Rasi. title: Chara Dasa — Dasa Rasi with Vipreet Argala (Counter-Intervention): Unfavourable Dasa
summary: When the active Chara Dasa Rasi is subjected to Vipreet Argala (counter-intervention that negates the Argala) rather than positive Argala, the Dasa will not be favourable.
full_text: In the Chara Dasa Argala-Vipreet Argala distinction logic (Slokas 53-55): Argala (intervention) refers to the mechanism by which planets in the 2nd, 4th, 5th, and 11th from a Rasi strengthen or promote its results. Vipreet Argala is the counter-intervention — when planets in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 12th from the Rasi obstruct and negate the positive Argala, the intervention is cancelled. The BPHS text states: 'The Dasa of the rasi, which is not aspected by auspicious Argala or of a rasi with Vipreet Argala, will not be favourable.' This rule establishes the negative counterpart to the positive Argala rule (rule 036): when the Dasa Rasi suffers Vipreet Argala — meaning its beneficial Argala is neutralised by counter-Argala planets — or when no positive Argala acts on it at all, the Dasa will be unfavourable. The engine must check the Argala-Vipreet Argala balance for each Dasa Rasi before finalising the period assessment. This rule was extracted directly from the BPHS PDF (Sloka 53-55) and was not captured in the NLM decode.

The 8th lord brings mortality-related and obstacle-type adversity; the 12th lord brings loss, isolation, and expenditure; the Sun, Mars, and Saturn bring their respective malefic significations into the Dasa Rasi's cycle. title: Antardasa Engine — Vimshottari Sub-period Duration Formula
summary: The duration of a Vimshottari Antardasa (sub-period) is calculated by: (Span of Main Dasa Years × Span of Target Dasa Years) ÷ 120, yielding the result in years, months, and days.
full_text: In the Vimshottari Dasa Antardasa computation engine: Slokas 1-2 establish the standard cross-multiplication formula for calculating the duration of each planetary sub-period (Antardasa) within a Vimshottari Dasa. The Antardasa sequence within any Dasa always begins from the sub-period of the same planet that owns the Main Dasa (the Dasa lord's own Antardasa is always first).

title: Ch51 Engine — Pratyantardasa Duration Formula: Antardasa Years × Target Planet Dasa Years ÷ Total Dasa Years
summary: The Pratyantardasa (sub-sub-period) duration is computed by multiplying the Antardasa years by the target planet's Dasa years and dividing the product by the total Dasa years (120 for Vimshottari), yielding months and days.
full_text: In the Vimshottari Pratyantardasa computation engine (Sloka 1, Notes section): the Chapter 51 opening sloka specifies both the Antardasa formula and the Pratyantardasa formula in a two-step computation. Step 1 (Antardasa): multiply the Dasa years of the Dasa planet by the Dasa years of the Antardasa planet, then divide by 120 (total Vimshottari years) — result is the Antardasa duration in years/months/days. Step 2 (Pratyantardasa): multiply the Antardasa years (as computed above) by the Dasa years of the planet whose Pratyantardasa is required, then divide by 120 — result is the Pratyantardasa duration in months/days. The BPHS notes provide a worked example: in the Dasa of Venus (20 years), the Antardasa of Venus is 20×20÷120 = 3 years 4 months. The Pratyantardasa of Venus within this is computed by multiplying 40 (the Antardasa numerator before dividing) by 20 (Venus Dasa years) = 9600, then dividing by 1440 (120×12 to convert) = 6 months 20 days. This rule was extracted directly from the BPHS PDF (Sloka 1 Notes, Ch51) and was not separately encoded in the NLM decode, which only specified the Antardasa formula.

title: Ch51 Engine — Bhoga Rasi Identification Algorithm: Same Distance from Dasa Rasi as Dasa Rasi is from Dasaprada
summary: When the Dasaprada Rasi is not the same as the Dasa Rasi (i.e., when the Antardasa sequence has progressed beyond the first Rasi), the Bhoga Rasi is identified as the Rasi that stands at the same distance from the Dasa Rasi as the Dasa Rasi stands from the Dasaprada Rasi.
full_text: In the Rasi Dasa Paka-Bhoga identification engine (Slokas 7-12, Notes): the identification of the Bhoga (Bahya) Rasi is a two-step algorithm. First, the Paka (Dwara) Rasi is identified: it is the Dasa Asraya Rasi — the Rasi currently under whose Dasa sub-period is being computed. Second, the Bhoga Rasi is identified using the following offset rule: 'If the Dasaprada Rasi be even, the Bhoga Rasi will be that which is at the same Rasi distance as the Dasa Asraya Rasi is from the Dasaprada Rasi.' In concrete terms: (1) Identify the first Dasaprada Rasi in the sequence (the starting Rasi of the Dasa); (2) Count how many Rasis forward (or backward, per direction rule) the current Paka Rasi stands from the Dasaprada Rasi — call this number N; (3) Count N Rasis forward (or backward) from the current Paka Rasi — the Rasi reached is the Bhoga Rasi. The worked example in the BPHS Notes confirms: for Aquarius Dasa (odd, so Aquarius is both Paka and Bhoga for the first Antardasa). For Pisces Antardasa (2nd from Aquarius Dasaprada), the Bhoga Rasi is the 2nd from Pisces = Aries. The BPHS also notes that Paka/Bhoga Rasis are alternatively called Dwara and Bahya Rasis. This algorithm was extracted directly from the BPHS PDF (Ch51 Notes section) and was not clearly encoded in the NLM decode.

title: Chara/Rasi Dasa — Adverse Antardasa Rasi: 6th, 8th, or 12th Placement or Malefic/Debilitated/Inimical Sign Occupation = Loss of Wealth, Disputes, Disease
summary: When the active Antardasa Rasi is the 6th, 8th, or 12th from the reference point, or when it is occupied by a malefic, a debilitated planet, or a planet in an inimical sign, the Antardasa produces inauspicious results including loss of wealth, disputes, and disease.
full_text: In the Chara Dasa Antardasa adverse-trigger logic (Slokas 92-93, Ch50 PDF): there will be inauspicious results — loss of wealth, disputes, and danger from disease — in the Antardasa of the Rasi which may be the 6th, the 8th, or the 12th (from the Dasa Rasi treated as Ascendant), or which is occupied by a malefic planet, a debilitated planet, or a planet housed in an inimical sign. Any one of these four conditions is sufficient to trigger the adverse Antardasa outcome. This is the negative counterpart to the positive Antardasa rule (own lord or friendly planet = kingdom/high office, rule bphs2-ch50-060).

This establishes a four-part adverse Antardasa gate: (1) Positional hazard — the Antardasa Rasi is the 6th, 8th, or 12th from the Dasa Rasi; (2) Malefic occupancy — a natural malefic planet resides in the Antardasa Rasi; (3) Debilitated occupancy — a debilitated planet resides in the Antardasa Rasi; (4) Inimical sign placement — a planet in the Antardasa Rasi is placed in a sign it considers inimical. Any one of these four conditions is sufficient to trigger the adverse Antardasa outcome. This is the negative counterpart to the positive Antardasa rule (own lord or friendly planet = kingdom/high office, rule bphs2-ch50-060).
interpretation.summary: When the active Antardasa Rasi is the 6th, 8th, or 12th from the reference point, or when it is occupied by a malefic, a debilitated planet, or a planet in an inimical sign, the Antardasa produces inauspicious results including loss of wealth, disputes, and disease.

title: Rasi Dasa — Paka and Bhoga Rasis Both Associated with Benefics: Enjoyment and Physical Well-Being
summary: When both the Paka (Dwara) Rasi and the Bhoga (Bahya) Rasi of the active Antardasa are associated with benefic planets, the sub-period produces enjoyment, physical well-being, and positive material experience.
full_text: In the Rasi Dasa Paka-Bhoga quality-assessment gate (Slokas 7-12): the BPHS establishes that the Paka and Bhoga Rasis act as a quality gateway for Rasi Dasa sub-periods. Rule bphs2-ch51-012 encodes the negative gate: Paka and Bhoga associated with malefics = pain in body and mental agony. This rule encodes the positive gate: when both the Paka (Dwara) Rasi and the Bhoga (Bahya) Rasi of the active Antardasa are associated with benefic planets — whether by occupancy or aspect — the Antardasa sub-period produces enjoyment and physical well-being. The BPHS text states: 'There will be enjoyment if they be associated with benefics.' The worked example in the Ch51 Notes confirms: in the Aquarius Dasa, Aquarius serves as both Paka and Bhoga for its own Antardasa. Since Aquarius is associated with benefics in the example horoscope, 'the native will be endowed with physical well being.' This positive Paka-Bhoga gate is the direct counterpart and mutual exclusive of the malefic Paka-Bhoga rule (rule bphs2-ch51-012). The engine must assess both Paka and Bhoga Rasi associations before issuing the quality verdict for each Antardasa sub-period.

result.effect: Enjoyment and physical well-being during the Antardasa sub-period — Paka and Bhoga Rasis both associated with benefics activates the positive quality gate.
